correctness.rationale: For distinct supports P and Q, a cyclic read at i differs exactly when i or i+1 is in T=P symmetric difference Q, so the distance is |T union (T-1)|. Disjoint supports have distance at least four. For supports with one common position, distance three occurs exactly when the two other positions are adjacent on the coordinate cycle. Consequently each neighborhood of the support graph must be cycle-independent, giving degree at most floor(n/2) and the claimed upper bound by summing degrees. The even-length parity graph attains the bound. At odd length 2k+1 with even k, the signed odd steps give circular gaps 2 and 3 and k neighbors. For odd k>=3, the smaller signed odd step set has a gap of 5; one displacement plus or minus k splits it into 2 and 3. A size-k matching of the step-k cycle supplies at most one such displacement per vertex (gcd(k,2k+1)=1), with total edge count (nk-1)/2. At k=1 it supplies a singleton code. Independent direct cyclic-read conflict enumeration at n=3 through 8 gave 1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 16, respectively; method and run record at /workspace/branches/0d375549-ae25-4fba-96cf-732b4ac3954e/record4-evidence.md. The symbolic reduction and constructions, not the finite enumeration, prove all lengths.

The unrelated unrestricted symbol-pair Singleton bound, where n>=4, is 2^(n-2) at distance four; it does not itself establish the exact restricted maximum.

evidence: Prior Theorem 1.3 gives floor(n*floor(n/2)/2), with F_2(C_3) isomorphic to C_3 and constructive cases for even n and both odd classes.

In the prior proof the layer L_i has linear separation n-i. For even n selecting odd-index layers gives exactly opposite-parity supports. For n=2k+1, the even-k layer selection gives precisely the signed odd steps through k-1. The odd-k selection takes the signed odd steps through k-2 and, additionally, the k disjoint pairs in L_k of cyclic step k. Thus the frozen constructions coincide with or re-express a prior extremizer (the arbitrary choice of maximum step-k matching is a variant, not a claimed classification).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both the exact scalar formula and the availability of explicit optimal constructions transfer through the support bijection. The prior proof also accounts for the parity split, not just an upper bound. The 2020 theorem and April 2026 corroboration give coverage independently of the later November account.

evidence: The vertices of F_2(C_n) are exactly the supports of the audited words. Two vertices are adjacent precisely when their symmetric difference is a single cycle edge, i.e. the two supports share one position and the two remaining positions are consecutive.
That adjacency is exactly pair-distance less than four for distinct weight-two words, without excluding adjacent supports or treating the two pair-weight layers separately.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The support map is a bijection and takes permissible codes to independent sets and back, preserving set size. This is exact equivalence, not a comparison to some denser unconstrained code family.

originality.rationale: The entire maximization is exactly the independence number of the two-token graph of a cycle. De Alba, Carballosa, Leaños and Rivera, Theorem 1.3 (2020), gives the identical formula, including n=3 and explicit extremizers in all parity classes. This is established prior coverage, independent of the unresolved coding papers.
